Solar Active Regions and flaring: Solar flaring activity was low over the past 24 hours. A single C-class flare was observed (SIDC Flare 8811, C1.1), peaking at 12:36 UTC on November 01. It was associated with SIDC Sunspot Group 976 (NOAA Active Region 4564, magnetic type beta). There are currently three numbered active regions on the solar disk. The most complex ones have a beta magnetic configuration. SIDC Sunspot Group 992 (magnetic type beta) has rotated on disk from the east limb, in the southeast quadrant. The solar flaring activity is expected to be low over the next 24 hours, with a chance for C-class.

Coronal mass ejections: A Coronal Mass Ejection (SIDC CME 739) was observed in LASCO/C2 and LASCO/C3 coronagraph imagery, starting from around 20:45 UTC on November 01, lifting off from the east limb. It is likely associated with eruptive activity behind the east limb, as seen by SUVI 195, starting from 18:45 UTC on November 01. It is not expected to impact Earth. SIDC CME
740 was observed in LASCO/C2 and LASCO/C3, starting from 19:00 UTC on November 01. It is likely associated with eruptive activity in the northeast quadrant, close to the central meridian, as seen by SUVI 195 and 304. A glancing blow may be expected to arrive at Earth starting from November 05. No other Earth-directed CMEs were observed in the available coronagraph imagery during the past 24 hours.

Solar wind: During the past 24 hours, the solar wind parameters (SOLAR-1 and ACE) reflected the waning influence of a high-speed stream from the equatorial, positive polarity coronal hole (SIDC Coronal Hole 179). The solar wind speed has decreased from 550 km/s to around 420 km/s. The interplanetary magnetic field was between 3 nT and 5 nT. The Bz component varied between -4 nT and 4 nT. The interplanetary magnetic field angle phi was initially mostly in the negative sector, switching to mostly positive around 06:00 UTC on November 02. Slow solar wind conditions are expected over the next 24 hours.

Geomagnetism: Geomagnetic conditions globally were at quiet to unsettled levels (NOAA Kp 2 to 3) during the past 24 hours. Geomagnetic conditions locally were mostly at unsettled levels (K Bel 3), with two isolated intervals of active levels (K Bel 4), between 15:00 and 16:00 UTC and between 20:00 and 21:00 UTC on November 01. Mostly quiet to unsettled conditions are expected over the next 24 hours, with possible isolated active intervals.

Proton flux levels: The greater than 10 MeV proton flux, as measured by GOES-18, was slightly enhanced but remained well below the 10 pfu threshold over the past 24 hours. It is expected to remain below the 10 pfu threshold over the next 24 hours.

Electron fluxes at GEO: The greater than 2 MeV electron flux measured by GOES 18 and GOES 19 exceeded the 1000 pfu threshold during the past 24 hours. The greater than 2 MeV electron flux is expected to cross the 1000 pfu threshold over the next 24 hours. The 24-hour electron fluence was at normal levels but it is expected to increase to moderate levels over the next 24 hours.

The source is a filament eruption spanning S12E15 to S20E30 which begins to lift off around 2026-10-12T04:45Z as seen in SDO 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. The arrival of this CME was observed at L1 by the SOLAR-1 spacecraft at 2026-10-14T17:28Z, characterized by an enhancement in magnetic field components (B_t: approx. 4.9nT to 7.3nt, B_x: approx. 4.8nT to -0.92nT, B_y: approx. -1.8nT to -6.5nT, B_z: approx. -2.0nT to 4.3nT), velocity (approx. 515km/s to 592km/s), density (approx. 4.9p/cc to 8.1 p/cc) and temperature (approx. 166kK to 273kK). This signature also exhibits a smoothening and slight rotation in magnetic field components, indicating the likely passage of a flux rope.
